body.translated_text: The <s>Śyāmalādaṇḍaka</s>, composed by the great poet <s>Śrī Kālidāsa</s>.

children.translated_text: She who plays upon a <s>vīṇā</s> of rubies, intoxicated and languid, with the charm of sweet speech,
her limbs soft as <s>mahendra-nīla</s> (great sapphire) — I constantly meditate upon the daughter of <s>Mātaṅga</s>.
Victory to the daughter of <s>Mātaṅga</s>! Victory to her who shines like a blue lotus!
Victory to her who delights in the essence of music! Victory to her who is fond of the playful parrot!

body.text:
jaya janani sudhāsamudrāntarudyanmaṇidvīpasaṃrūḍhabilvāṭavīmadhyakalpadrumākalpakādambakāntāravāsapriye kṛttivāsaḥpriye sarvalokapriye /
sādarārabdhasaṃgītasaṃbhāvanāsaṃbhramālolanīpasragābaddhacūlīsanāthatrike sānumatputrike /
śekharībhūtapītāṃśurekhāmayūkhāvalībaddhasusnigdhanīlālakaśreṇiśṛṅgārite lokasaṃbhāvite /
kāmalīlādhanuḥsaṃnibhabhrūlatāpuṣpasaṃdohasaṃdehakṛllocane vāksudhāsecane /
cārugorocanāpaṅkakelīlalāmābhirāme surāme rame /
prollasadbālikāmauktikaśreṇikācandrikāmaṇḍalodbhāsilāvaṇyagaṇḍasthalanyastakastūrikāpattrarekhāsamudbhūtasaurabhyasaṃbhrāntabhṛṅgāṅganāgītasāndrībhavanmandratantrīsvare susvare bhāsvare /
vallakīvādanaprakriyālolatālīdalābaddhatāṭaṅkabhūṣāviśeṣānvite siddhasaṃmānite /

children.translated_text: you whose sidelong glances, languid and rolling with the intoxication of divine liquor (<s>hālā</s>), whose beauty matches a single blue lotus placed at the ear, O one who fulfills all the wishes of the world, O <s>Śrīphala</s> (auspicious fruit);
you whose nose-pearl creates the doubt of being a drop of perspiration glistening on the beautiful forehead, exuding loveliness; O soul of the entire universe, O <s>Kālikā</s>;

you from whose radiant mouth, graced with a gentle, innocent smile, arise heaps of betel, <s>tāmbūla</s>, and camphor fragments; you whose hand displays the <s>jñānamudrā</s> (gesture of knowledge), who grants all prosperity, whose hand shines like a lotus;

you whose row of smooth teeth gleaming like <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) blossoms, whose pure radiance merges with a smiling lower lip of lovely red — O bearer of the beautiful <s>vīṇā</s>, O one whose lip is like a ripe <s>bimba</s> fruit! [Verse 1]

body.text:
sulalitanavayauvanārambhacandrodayodvelalāvaṇyadugdhārṇavāvirbhavatkambubibbokabhṛtkaṃdhare satkalāmandire manthare /
divyaratnaprabhābandhuracchannahārādibhūṣāsamuddyotamānānavadyāṃśuśobhe śubhe /
ratnakeyūraraśmicchaṭāpallavaprollasaddorlatārājite yogibhiḥ pūjite /
viśvadiṅmaṇḍalavyāpimāṇikyatejaḥsphuratkaṅkaṇālaṃkṛte vibhramālaṃkṛte sādhakaiḥ satkṛte /
vāsarārambhavelāsamujjṛmbhamānāravindapratidvandvipāṇidvaye saṃtatodyaddaye advaye /
divyaratnormikādīdhitistomasaṃdhyāyamānāṅgulīpallavodyannakhenduprabhāmaṇḍale saṃnatākhaṇḍale citprabhāmaṇḍale prollasatkuṇḍale /
tārakārājinīkāśahārāvalismeracārustanābhogabhārānamanmadhyavallībalicchedavīcīsamullāsasaṃdarśitākārasaundaryaratnākare vallakībhṛtkare kiṃkaraśrīkare /

children.translated_text: you who bend with the weight of the high breasts resembling golden water-pots, before whom the three worlds bow;
you adorned by the row of dark body-hair creating the illusion of moss on the bank of the lake of the deep, round navel; O one of sweet conversation;
you whose tinkling girdle-string puts to shame the bowstring of the playful bow of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Bodiless Kāma) in its jingling; clad in divine gem-studded garments;
you whose hips, brilliant with the radiance of gleaming <s>padmarāga</s> (ruby) girdle, whose beauty defeats the golden mountain; O one cool as moonlight! [Verse 2]

you whose beautiful thighs, concealed by divine crimson silks red as blossoming fresh <s>kiṃśuka</s> flowers, vanquish the shame-reddened trunks of <s>Indra</s>'s elephants; O one of unmatched splendor, O <s>Śyāmalā</s>;
you whose graceful shanks give rise to the suspicion that they are the quiver of <s>Anaṅga</s>, [being] smooth, delicate, and dark as blue sapphire; O one of charming playful gait;

you whose toenail-moons gleam brightly, creating the suspicion of <s>dūrvā</s> (sacred grass) sprouts, in the smooth dark luster of the tresses of the wives of the bowing guardians of the directions — touching, grazing, causing the appearance of a deer; O one brilliantly radiant, O stainless one;

you whose lotus feet are reddened by the lac-like crimson dawn of the fierce rays of the sun, rubbed against by the jewel-crests of the bowing lords — <s>Deveśa</s> (Indra), <s>Lakṣmīśa</s> (Viṣṇu), <s>Bhūteśa</s> (Śiva), <s>Toyeśa</s> (Varuṇa), <s>Vāṇīśa</s> (Brahmā), <s>Kīnāśa</s> (Yama), <s>Daityeśa</s>, <s>Yakṣeśa</s> (Kubera), <s>Vāyu</s>, and <s>Agni</s> — the youthful beauty embodied in redness; O one of beautiful lotus feet, O <s>Umā</s>! [Verse 3]

body.text:
suruciranavaratnapīṭhasthite susthite /
ratnapadmāsane ratnasiṃhāsane śaṅkhapadmadvayopāśrite /
tatra vighneśadurgābaṭukṣetrapālairyute /
mattamātaṅgakanyāsamūhānvite mañjulāmenakādyaṅganāmānite bhairavairaṣṭabhirveṣṭite /
devi vāmādibhiḥ śaktibhiḥ sevite /
dhātrilakṣmyādiśaktyaṣṭakaiḥ saṃyute /
mātṛkāmaṇḍalairmaṇḍite /
yakṣagandharvasiddhāṅganāmaṇḍalairarcite /
pañcabāṇātmike /
pañcabāṇena ratyā na saṃbhāvite /
prītibhājā vasantena cānandite /
bhaktibhājaṃ paraṃ śreyase kalpase /
yogināṃ mānase dyotase /

children.translated_text: you blaze with the power of sacred meters,
you are worshipped by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who delights beyond measure in the art of music,
you are praised by <s>Brahmā</s> (the Creator) with a devoted heart,
you are sung by <s>Vidyādharas</s> with music that delights the whole world. // 4 //

body.translated_text:
Seated upon a beautiful throne of nine gems, well-established,
upon a lotus-seat of jewels, upon a lion-throne of jewels, attended by the pair [of emblems] conch and lotus,
there accompanied by <s>Vighneśa</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Baṭuka</s>, and the guardians of the field,
surrounded by a host of intoxicated elephant-maidens, honored by the beautiful <s>Menakā</s> and other celestial women, encircled by the eight <s>Bhairavas</s>,
O Goddess, served by <s>Vāmā</s> and other <s>Śaktis</s>,
united with the eight <s>Śaktis</s> headed by <s>Dhātrī</s> and <s>Lakṣmī</s>,
adorned by the circles of <s>Mātṛkās</s> (Mother-Goddesses),
worshipped by circles of <s>Yakṣa</s>, <s>Gandharva</s>, and <s>Siddha</s> maidens,
embodying the five arrows [of <s>Kāma</s>],
honored by <s>Kāmadeva</s> (the Five-Arrowed One) together with <s>Rati</s>,
delighted by <s>Vasanta</s> (Spring), who shares in your joy—
you bestow the highest good upon those devoted to you,
you shine in the minds of <s>yogins</s>,

body.text:
śravaṇaharaṇadakṣiṇakvāṇayā vīṇayā kiṃnarairgīyase /
yakṣagandharvasiddhaṅganāmaṇḍalairarcyase /
sarvasaubhāgyavāñchāvatībhirvadhūbhiḥ surāṇāṃ samārādhyase /
sarvavidyāviśeṣātmakaṃ cāṭugāthāsamuccāraṇaṃ kaṇṭhamūlollasadvarṇarājitrayaṃ komalaśyāmalodārapakṣadvayaṃ tuṇḍaśobhātidūrībhavatkiṃśukaṃ taṃ śukaṃ lālayantī parikrīḍase /
pāṇipadmadvayenākṣamālāmapi sphāṭikīṃ jñānasārātmakaṃ pustakaṃ cāṅkuśaṃ pāśamābibhratī yena saṃcintyase tasya vaktrāntarādgadyapadyātmikā bhāratī niḥsaret /
yena vā yāvakābhākṛtirbhāvyase tasya vaśyā bhavanti striyaḥ pūruṣāḥ /

children.text: yena vā śātakumbhadyutirbhāvyase so 'pi lakṣmīsahasraiḥ parikrīḍate /
children.translated_text: whoever contemplates your form of golden radiance, he too sports with thousands of <s>Lakṣmīs</s> (fortunes).

children.text: kiṃ na siddhyedvapuḥ śyāmalaṃ komalaṃ candracūḍānvitaṃ tāvakaṃ dhyāyataḥ /
children.translated_text: What would not be accomplished by one who meditates upon your body—dark, soft, adorned with the crescent moon upon the crest?

children.text: tasya līlāsaro vāridhistasya kelīvanaṃ candanaṃ tasya bhadrāsanaṃ bhūtalaṃ tasya gīrdevatā kiṃkarī tasya cājñākarī śrīḥ svayam /
children.translated_text: For him, the ocean is a playful lake; the sandalwood grove is his pleasure-garden; the surface of the earth is his comfortable seat; <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the Goddess of Speech, is his servant; and <s>Śrī</s> (the Goddess of Fortune) herself obeys his command.

children.text: sarvatīrthātmike sarvamantrātmike sarvatantrātmike sarvayantrātmike sarvaśaktyātmike sarvapīṭhātmike sarvatattvātmike sarvavidyātmike sarvayogātmike sarvanādātmike sarvaśabdātmike sarvaviśvātmike sarvadīkṣātmike sarvasarvātmike sarvage pāhi māṃ pāhi māṃ pāhi māṃ devi tubhyaṃ namo devi tubhyaṃ namo devi tubhyaṃ namaḥ // 5 //
children.translated_text: O you who are the essence of all <s>tīrthas</s> (sacred waters), all <s>mantras</s>, all <s>tantras</s>, all <s>yantras</s>, all <s>śaktis</s> (powers), all <s>pīṭhas</s> (sacred seats), all <s>tattvas</s> (principles), all <s>vidyās</s> (knowledge-sciences), all <s>yogas</s>, all <s>nādas</s> (sounds), all <s>śabdas</s> (words), all the universe, all <s>dīkṣās</s> (initiations), and the essence of all—O all-pervading one, protect me, protect me, protect me! O Goddess, homage to you! O Goddess, homage to you! O Goddess, homage to you! // 5 //
May the Mother, dark as emerald, <s>Mātaṅgī</s>, glorious in intoxication,
the auspicious one dwelling in the <s>kadamba</s> forest, cast her sidelong glance [upon me].

body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Śyāmalādaṇḍaka</s> composed by the great poet Śrī <s>Kālidāsa</s> is completed.
